name: PageHeader
label: Page header
description: The top of a page: its breadcrumb, title, description and actions, folding the actions under the text when narrow.

props.name: title
props.description:
The page's title, its heading.
Note: this shadows the native `title` tooltip attribute, which PageHeader does not expose.

props.name: description
props.description: A sentence under the title on what the page is for or what it holds.

props.name: breadcrumb
props.description: The trail above the title, from the top of the app to this page; the last item is this page and takes no `href`.

props.name: actions
props.description: The page's own actions at the end of the title row: one primary Button, a secondary or two. On a narrow page they take the row under the text.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: The heading's place in the outline. The page's title is its `h1`; a header inside a tab or a pane can be an `h2`.

props.name: linkComponent
props.description:
The component the breadcrumb's links render with, such as Next.js's
`Link`, so they navigate through the app's router; a plain `<a>` when
unset. This component can render on the server, so it never reads a
LinkProvider: pass the prop even under one.

LinkComponent.description: A component that renders a link in place of a plain `<a>`, such as a router's.

LinkComponentProps.description:
The props a link component receives: every anchor attribute, the ref, and
an `href` that is always a string. Next.js's `Link` takes these as they
are; a router whose link takes `to` instead needs a one-line adapter:
`({ href, ...props }) => <RouterLink to={href} {...props} />`.

keys.note: Its breadcrumb links and the actions passed in are native links and buttons, reached with Tab.

alternatives.name: SectionTitle
alternatives.when: the heading opens a section within a page rather than the page itself
